title: GitHub - blumalex/eso-box: Turn a spare Linux PC or Mac into an always-on box: open sessions from any laptop over SSH, carry them on from your phone in the Claude app. Keeps running when you disconnect, and comes back by itself after a crash or power cut.

content_html:
Carry your Claude Code sessions across all your devices. An always-on machine at home (the "box") runs your Claude Code sessions. Your laptop opens them over SSH, your phone through the Claude app, and you can switch between them mid-conversation: start on the laptop, carry on from the phone, finish on the laptop.

eso-box is a small set of scripts and settings on top of tmux, Tailscale and Claude Code's own features. It is not affiliated with Anthropic.

Features

  • Your real setup. Claude works with your data, secrets, running dev servers and signed-in tools.
  • The same live session, on any device. Pick it up from any laptop over SSH (bash, zsh or PowerShell, on Windows, macOS or Linux), or from your phone in the Claude app.
  • Start on your phone, finish at your desk. Start new sessions on the box from the Claude app, then continue them in a terminal: /resume lists them as ☏ · <the phone's title>.
  • It keeps going. Close every device and the work continues.
  • A box that looks after itself. It never sleeps (lid closed is fine), reboots itself after a freeze, comes back after a power cut, and reconnects to your phone after network outages. (Linux; macOS untested.)
  • Tabs that tell you what's happening. Each session keeps Claude's title for it on every device, a phone-started one keeps the phone's title in a terminal, and names you set with /rename stick. Its tab shows ◐ while Claude works and ✳ when it's done or waiting on you.
  • Try your app on your phone. Open it against the box's dev server.
  • Private by default. Every device reaches the box over Tailscale, with no ports open on your router. With --firewall, a Linux box accepts connections only from your devices.
  • Nothing new to trust. It's just tmux, Tailscale and Claude Code's own Remote Control, and every script is short enough to read.

How it works

  Windows / macOS / Linux laptop ──ssh (Tailscale)──┐
                                                    ▼
                         box (Linux or macOS):  tmux ─▶ claude ◀── Remote Control ── Claude app (iOS, Android)
                                                                                     or claude.ai/code (any browser)

The session never moves. It runs on the box inside tmux with Claude Code's Remote Control on. The laptop attaches to the tmux session, and the phone attaches through Remote Control. Both see and drive the same Claude.

How is this different from claude --cloud?

Cloud sessions work on a copy of your project, on Anthropic's machines. eso-box lets you work on your project from anywhere, on your own machine.

A cloud session (claude --cloud, or claude.ai/code) runs on a fresh Anthropic VM with a clean clone of your GitHub repo. eso-box runs your sessions on your own machine, in your real setup.

Cloud session eso-box
Your setup A fresh clone, rebuilt by a setup script: no untracked files, local .env files, databases or signed-in tools Already there
Moving to a terminal --teleport makes a copy that doesn't sync back The same live session, both ways
Dev servers and long jobs An idle session's VM pauses after a few minutes and can be reclaimed, along with anything running Keep running
Your app on your phone No way to reach the VM Open the box's dev server
Networks Public sites you allow; not your LAN, VPN or tailnet Anything the box can reach
Hardware About 4 vCPUs, 16 GB of RAM, no GPU Yours
Your code Copied to Anthropic's VM; GitHub access through the Claude GitHub App or your gh token Stays on your disk; only what Claude reads or runs goes to Anthropic
Isolation A separate VM per task, with credentials kept outside it None: Claude works with your own logins and access
Upkeep None A machine you keep on and secure

Use cloud sessions for self-contained tasks and for running many at once, and the box for the project you work in every day. They combine: run claude --cloud from the box to hand off a side task.

Anthropic's docs point here too: "To run Claude Code on your own always-on machine and drive it from other devices, use Remote Control" (self-hosted environments), and for work beyond the cloud VM's limits, "use Remote Control to run Claude Code on your own hardware" (cloud environments).

What's in it

Path What it does
box/linux/setup-root.sh System settings for running unattended: never sleep, ignore the lid, reboot by itself after a crash or freeze, skip the boot menu wait after a power cut, battery charge limit on laptops, optional tailnet-only firewall
box/macos/setup-root.sh The same for a Mac (Mac mini). Untested
install.sh Installs the tools, tab titles and hooks, and runs Claude Code's Remote Control server as a service so sessions started from the phone run on the box
bin/eso-session What box runs on the box: opens or creates a tmux session running Claude
bin/eso-rc-loop Keeps the Remote Control server running (it exits after ~10 min without network)
bin/eso-rc-title Hook: the phone's session list shows Claude's own title for each session
bin/eso-phone Lists sessions started from the phone, with the /resume line that continues one in a terminal
bin/eso-phone-sync Hook: /resume lists sessions started from the phone, named ☏ · <the phone's title>
config/tmux.conf Terminal tab shows ◐ <Claude's title> · <session> while working, ✳ when done
client/box.sh, client/box.ps1 box and boxls for bash/zsh (Linux, macOS, WSL, Termux) and PowerShell

Status

  • Linux box: tested on Ubuntu Desktop 26.04 (a ThinkPad laptop with the lid closed), with Claude Code 2.1.32x, for days of daily use, overnight runs, power cuts and reboots. The scripts here are generalized from that setup.
  • macOS box: untested. Written from Apple's documented settings; see docs/gotchas.md for what to check first. Reports welcome.
  • Windows as the box: not supported yet (WSL2, Windows sleep, no Tailscale SSH server). Windows works fine as a client.
  • Clients: Windows (WSL bash and PowerShell), Linux, macOS, Android (Claude app; Termux for SSH), iPhone and iPad (Claude app; any SSH app).

What you need

  • A Claude subscription that includes Remote Control, signed in with your claude.ai account (not an API key).
  • A free Tailscale account: every device reaches the box over your private tailnet, with no ports opened on your router.
  • The box: a machine that can stay on. A spare laptop works (the battery rides out short power cuts); a Mac mini works if you accept the FileVault tradeoff in docs/security.md.

Set up the box

install.sh backs up your Claude settings and tmux config before changing them, adds its hooks next to yours, and is safe to rerun.

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

  1. Install the OS. For a desktop you can use over remote desktop, enable automatic login. Read docs/security.md before choosing disk encryption: a passphrase prompt blocks unattended boot after a power cut.
  2. In the BIOS, turn on "power on with AC attach" (or "restore on AC power loss"), so the box boots by itself when power returns.
  3. Tailscale: curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh, then sudo tailscale up --ssh. In the admin console, open the box's menu and Disable key expiry (otherwise it drops off the tailnet after 180 days).
  4. Claude Code: install it, then run claude once in your project folder, sign in, and accept the trust question.
  5. eso-box: 
    git clone https://github.com/blumalex/eso-box ~/eso-box && cd ~/eso-box
sudo box/linux/setup-root.sh            # add --firewall once you're connected over Tailscale
./install.sh --dir ~/code/myproject
sudo systemctl reboot -i

macOS (untested)

  1. System Settings > Users & Groups: automatic login (needs FileVault off; see docs/security.md).
  2. Homebrew, then brew install tmux jq tailscale. For Tailscale SSH use this open-source tailscaled (sudo brew services start tailscale, sudo tailscale up --ssh); the App Store app can't run an SSH server. Or turn on Remote Login and use SSH keys.
  3. Claude Code, as in step 4 above.
  4. eso-box: clone it, then sudo box/macos/setup-root.sh and ./install.sh --dir ~/code/myproject.

Set up each device

Install Tailscale on each device and sign in to the same tailnet. Then:

Device Terminal Phone-style
Windows PowerShell: add $env:ESO_BOX_HOST = 'mybox' and . "$HOME\eso-box\client\box.ps1" to $PROFILE. Or WSL, as Linux claude.ai/code in a browser
macOS, Linux Add export ESO_BOX_HOST=mybox and . ~/eso-box/client/box.sh to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc claude.ai/code in a browser
Android Termux (pkg install openssh), then as Linux Claude app
iPhone, iPad Any SSH app: ssh mybox -t '~/.local/bin/eso-session 3' Claude app

mybox is the box's Tailscale name; use user@mybox if your user name there differs. Only the laptop needs this repo, for the client file. In Claude Code's /config on the box, turn on Push when actions required so permission prompts reach your phone.

Daily use

  • box: a new Claude session on the box. tmux numbers them 0, 1, 2...
  • box 3: back into session 3 (or a new one named 3). boxls lists them with Claude's titles.
  • Close the window to leave a session running; it keeps working with the laptop asleep. Quitting Claude (Ctrl+C twice) ends the session.
  • Phone: every session on the box appears in the Claude app. Type in either place.
  • Sessions started from the phone run on the box too. To continue one in a terminal, once: let Claude finish its turn, run box, type /resume and pick its ☏ · <title> entry. From then on use the terminal session's own entry on the phone. See docs/using.md.

Docs

  • docs/using.md: the flows step by step, and what happens when the network, power or the laptop goes away
  • docs/gotchas.md: what we ran into and how it's handled
  • docs/background-sessions.md: Claude Code's own background sessions (claude agents) as an alternative to tmux
  • docs/security.md: the tradeoffs, and what to revoke if the box is stolen

Limitations

  • eso-phone, eso-rc-title and eso-phone-sync read Claude Code's transcript files, an internal format that can change between versions. If they stop working after an update, the rest still works. eso-phone-sync also edits them: in each phone session's file it changes the one mark that hides it from /resume (in place, same length, logged to ~/.local/state/eso-phone-sync.log) and appends a name.
  • The phone's title for a phone-started session comes from an internal claude.ai API, as Claude Code itself calls it (untested on a Mac box). Without it, that session's terminal tab just says "Claude Code".
  • tmux sessions don't survive a reboot. The conversations do: box, then claude --continue or /resume.
  • The Remote Control server serves one project folder. Sessions you start with box can cd anywhere.

License

MIT

content_html_zh:
Carry your Claude Code sessions across all your devices. An always-on machine at home (the "box") runs your Claude Code sessions. Your laptop opens them over SSH, your phone through the Claude app, and you can switch between them mid-conversation: start on the laptop, carry on from the phone, finish on the laptop.

eso-box is a small set of scripts and settings on top of tmux, Tailscale and Claude Code's own features. It is not affiliated with Anthropic.

特征

  • Your real setup. Claude works with your data, secrets, running dev servers and signed-in tools.
  • The same live session, on any device. Pick it up from any laptop over SSH (bash, zsh or PowerShell, on Windows, macOS or Linux), or from your phone in the Claude app.
  • Start on your phone, finish at your desk. Start new sessions on the box from the Claude app, then continue them in a terminal: /resume lists them as ☏ · <the phone's title>.
  • It keeps going. Close every device and the work continues.
  • A box that looks after itself. It never sleeps (lid closed is fine), reboots itself after a freeze, comes back after a power cut, and reconnects to your phone after network outages. (Linux; macOS untested.)
  • Tabs that tell you what's happening. Each session keeps Claude's title for it on every device, a phone-started one keeps the phone's title in a terminal, and names you set with /rename stick. Its tab shows ◐ while Claude works and ✳ when it's done or waiting on you.
  • Try your app on your phone. Open it against the box's dev server.
  • 默认为私有。 Every device reaches the box over Tailscale, with no ports open on your router. With --firewall, a Linux box accepts connections only from your devices.
  • Nothing new to trust. It's just tmux, Tailscale and Claude Code's own Remote Control, and every script is short enough to read.

它是如何运作的

  Windows / macOS / Linux laptop ──ssh (Tailscale)──┐
                                                    ▼
                         box (Linux or macOS):  tmux ─▶ claude ◀── Remote Control ── Claude app (iOS, Android)
                                                                                     or claude.ai/code (any browser)

The session never moves. It runs on the box inside tmux with Claude Code's Remote Control on. The laptop attaches to the tmux session, and the phone attaches through Remote Control. Both see and drive the same Claude.

How is this different from claude --cloud?

Cloud sessions work on a copy of your project, on Anthropic's machines. eso-box lets you work on your project from anywhere, on your own machine.

A cloud session (claude --cloud, or claude.ai/code) runs on a fresh Anthropic VM with a clean clone of your GitHub repo. eso-box runs your sessions on your own machine, in your real setup.

Cloud session eso-box
Your setup A fresh clone, rebuilt by a setup script: no untracked files, local .env files, databases or signed-in tools Already there
Moving to a terminal --teleport makes a copy that doesn't sync back The same live session, both ways
Dev servers and long jobs An idle session's VM pauses after a few minutes and can be reclaimed, along with anything running Keep running
Your app on your phone No way to reach the VM Open the box's dev server
网络 Public sites you allow; not your LAN, VPN or tailnet Anything the box can reach
硬件 About 4 vCPUs, 16 GB of RAM, no GPU Yours
你的代码 Copied to Anthropic's VM; GitHub access through the Claude GitHub App or your gh token Stays on your disk; only what Claude reads or runs goes to Anthropic
隔离 A separate VM per task, with credentials kept outside it None: Claude works with your own logins and access
Upkeep None A machine you keep on and secure

Use cloud sessions for self-contained tasks and for running many at once, and the box for the project you work in every day. They combine: run claude --cloud from the box to hand off a side task.

Anthropic's docs point here too: "To run Claude Code on your own always-on machine and drive it from other devices, use Remote Control" (self-hosted environments), and for work beyond the cloud VM's limits, "use Remote Control to run Claude Code on your own hardware" (cloud environments).

里面有什么

Path 它的作用
box/linux/setup-root.sh System settings for running unattended: never sleep, ignore the lid, reboot by itself after a crash or freeze, skip the boot menu wait after a power cut, battery charge limit on laptops, optional tailnet-only firewall
box/macos/setup-root.sh The same for a Mac (Mac mini). Untested
install.sh Installs the tools, tab titles and hooks, and runs Claude Code's Remote Control server as a service so sessions started from the phone run on the box
bin/eso-session What box runs on the box: opens or creates a tmux session running Claude
bin/eso-rc-loop Keeps the Remote Control server running (it exits after ~10 min without network)
bin/eso-rc-title Hook: the phone's session list shows Claude's own title for each session
bin/eso-phone Lists sessions started from the phone, with the /resume line that continues one in a terminal
bin/eso-phone-sync Hook: /resume lists sessions started from the phone, named ☏ · <the phone's title>
config/tmux.conf Terminal tab shows ◐ <Claude's title> · <session> while working, ✳ when done
client/box.sh, client/box.ps1 box and boxls for bash/zsh (Linux, macOS, WSL, Termux) and PowerShell

地位

  • Linux box: tested on Ubuntu Desktop 26.04 (a ThinkPad laptop with the lid closed), with Claude Code 2.1.32x, for days of daily use, overnight runs, power cuts and reboots. The scripts here are generalized from that setup.
  • macOS box: untested. Written from Apple's documented settings; see docs/gotchas.md for what to check first. Reports welcome.
  • Windows as the box: not supported yet (WSL2, Windows sleep, no Tailscale SSH server). Windows works fine as a client.
  • Clients: Windows (WSL bash and PowerShell), Linux, macOS, Android (Claude app; Termux for SSH), iPhone and iPad (Claude app; any SSH app).

你需要什么

  • A Claude subscription that includes Remote Control, signed in with your claude.ai account (not an API key).
  • A free Tailscale account: every device reaches the box over your private tailnet, with no ports opened on your router.
  • The box: a machine that can stay on. A spare laptop works (the battery rides out short power cuts); a Mac mini works if you accept the FileVault tradeoff in docs/security.md.

Set up the box

install.sh backs up your Claude settings and tmux config before changing them, adds its hooks next to yours, and is safe to rerun.

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu)

  1. Install the OS. For a desktop you can use over remote desktop, enable automatic login. Read docs/security.md before choosing disk encryption: a passphrase prompt blocks unattended boot after a power cut.
  2. In the BIOS, turn on "power on with AC attach" (or "restore on AC power loss"), so the box boots by itself when power returns.
  3. Tailscale: curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh, then sudo tailscale up --ssh. In the admin console, open the box's menu and Disable key expiry (otherwise it drops off the tailnet after 180 days).
  4. Claude Code: install it, then run claude once in your project folder, sign in, and accept the trust question.
  5. eso-box: git clone https://github.com/blumalex/eso-box ~/eso-box && cd ~/eso-box sudo box/linux/setup-root.sh # add --firewall once you're connected over Tailscale ./install.sh --dir ~/code/myproject sudo systemctl reboot -i

macOS (untested)

  1. System Settings > Users & Groups: automatic login (needs FileVault off; see docs/security.md).
  2. Homebrew, then brew install tmux jq tailscale. For Tailscale SSH use this open-source tailscaled (sudo brew services start tailscale, sudo tailscale up --ssh); the App Store app can't run an SSH server. Or turn on Remote Login and use SSH keys.
  3. Claude Code, as in step 4 above.
  4. eso-box: clone it, then sudo box/macos/setup-root.sh and ./install.sh --dir ~/code/myproject.

Set up each device

Install Tailscale on each device and sign in to the same tailnet. 然后：

设备 终端 Phone-style
视窗 PowerShell: add $env:ESO_BOX_HOST = 'mybox' and . "$HOME\eso-box\client\box.ps1" to $PROFILE. Or WSL, as Linux claude.ai/code in a browser
macOS、Linux Add export ESO_BOX_HOST=mybox and . ~/eso-box/client/box.sh to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc claude.ai/code in a browser
安卓 Termux (pkg install openssh), then as Linux Claude app
iPhone, iPad Any SSH app: ssh mybox -t '~/.local/bin/eso-session 3' Claude app

mybox is the box's Tailscale name; use user@mybox if your user name there differs. Only the laptop needs this repo, for the client file. In Claude Code's /config on the box, turn on Push when actions required so permission prompts reach your phone.

Daily use

  • box: a new Claude session on the box. tmux numbers them 0, 1, 2...
  • box 3: back into session 3 (or a new one named 3). boxls lists them with Claude's titles.
  • Close the window to leave a session running; it keeps working with the laptop asleep. Quitting Claude (Ctrl+C twice) ends the session.
  • Phone: every session on the box appears in the Claude app. Type in either place.
  • Sessions started from the phone run on the box too. To continue one in a terminal, once: let Claude finish its turn, run box, type /resume and pick its ☏ · <title> entry. From then on use the terminal session's own entry on the phone. See docs/using.md.

Docs

  • docs/using.md: the flows step by step, and what happens when the network, power or the laptop goes away
  • docs/gotchas.md: what we ran into and how it's handled
  • docs/background-sessions.md: Claude Code's own background sessions (claude agents) as an alternative to tmux
  • docs/security.md: the tradeoffs, and what to revoke if the box is stolen

局限性

  • eso-phone, eso-rc-title and eso-phone-sync read Claude Code's transcript files, an internal format that can change between versions. If they stop working after an update, the rest still works. eso-phone-sync also edits them: in each phone session's file it changes the one mark that hides it from /resume (in place, same length, logged to ~/.local/state/eso-phone-sync.log) and appends a name.
  • The phone's title for a phone-started session comes from an internal claude.ai API, as Claude Code itself calls it (untested on a Mac box). Without it, that session's terminal tab just says "Claude Code".
  • tmux sessions don't survive a reboot. The conversations do: box, then claude --continue or /resume.
  • The Remote Control server serves one project folder. Sessions you start with box can cd anywhere.
